meta.title: Algolia for Dell — Search that matches your scale
meta.description: A personalized look at what Algolia AI Search could do for Dell.com, grounded in PRISM's audit of dell.com search.

hero.sub: PRISM audited dell.com's live search experience. Here's what closing the gap with Algolia AI Search could be worth to Dell — and what's holding it back today.

roi.heading: What closing the search gap is worth
roi.subheading: Three scenarios, built from Dell's own public revenue figures — not industry averages.

cards.label: Conservative
cards.desc: Conversion lift + bounce reduction on direct ecommerce only.

cards.label: Moderate
cards.desc: Full suite: conversion + bounce + no-results recovery + long-tail discovery.

cards.label: Best case
cards.desc: Full suite + AOV lift + personalization. Requires deal-team validation.

roi.note: Source: PRISM audit, Dell Technologies FY2025 investor relations (2026-02-27) + ecommercedb.com estimate (2026-03-26). Best-case scenario needs AE sizing before use in a proposal.

findings.heading: Four gaps in dell.com search today
findings.subheading: Observed directly on dell.com, not inferred.

items.title: Every visitor sees the same results
items.body: No signal from browsing history, account tier, or B2B vs. B2C context shapes what dell.com search shows. Algolia AI Search personalizes ranking per shopper without extra engineering lift.

items.title: Natural-language queries don't resolve
items.body: Shoppers searching in plain language ("laptop for video editing under $1500") get literal keyword matching, not intent. Algolia's Neural Search understands intent without a rules engine to maintain.

items.title: Autocomplete has no visual guidance
items.body: No product images, categories, or merchandised suggestions appear while typing — a missed moment to guide Dell's complex catalog. Rich SAYT cuts time-to-product materially in comparable B2B catalogs.

items.title: A dead end, not a redirect
items.body: Zero-result searches don't recover the shopper — no typo correction, no related-category fallback. Every dead-end is a shopper Dell already paid to acquire, walking away.

capabilities.heading: The platform behind the fix
capabilities.sub: Not a one-time integration — a system Dell's team keeps improving.
